name: Dhaka
description: The capital — Mughal forts, Old Dhaka lanes, river ports and the busiest food scene in the country.

name: Chattogram
description: Port city between hills and sea — Patenga beach, Foy’s Lake and the coastal hills of Sitakunda.

name: Sylhet
description: Rolling tea gardens, the Ratargul swamp forest and the clear stone-bed rivers of Jaflong and Bisnakandi.

name: Khulna
description: Gateway to the Sundarbans and home of the UNESCO-listed mosque city of Bagerhat.

name: Rajshahi
description: Clean, green “Silk City” on the Padma — terracotta temples of Puthia, mango orchards and Rajshahi silk.

name: Rangpur
description: Northern city known for the Tajhat Palace and the legacy of Begum Rokeya.

name: Barishal
description: The “Venice of Bengal” — river life, floating guava markets and the Guthia Mosque.

name: Cumilla
description: Ancient Buddhist ruins of Mainamati, a WWII war cemetery and the famous Cumillar Rosh Malai.

name: Mymensingh
description: Quiet river town on the old Brahmaputra with zamindar palaces and the Zainul Abedin art museum.

name: Cox's Bazar
description: The world’s longest natural sea beach, with the Marine Drive, Himchari hills and Inani’s coral stones.

name: Sajek Valley
description: Hilltop village in Rangamati above a sea of clouds — reached by jeep from Khagrachhari.

name: Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest on Earth and home of the Royal Bengal Tiger, explored by boat from Khulna or Mongla.
